title: Caleb at eighty-five (Joshua 14:6–15)
hookLine: the old scout says he's as strong as ever: "give me this mountain"
last: A PLACE CAN BE A CALLING.

lines: GILGAL: THE LAND IS SHARED OUT.
cards: Eighty-five years old, and he's asking for ground held by giants. The people of Judah have come to Joshua at Gilgal, where the land is being shared out. One old man steps forward with a story.
Forty years old was I, he says, when Moses sent me to spy out this land. I brought back word as it was in my heart. The others made the people's hearts melt.
I didn't. Then he names his age today. And then he makes a request, and it isn't for a quiet valley.

teach.b: In the wilderness, at Kadesh-barnea, Moses sent scouts into this land. The book of Numbers tells it: the others came back talking about walled cities and giants, the sons of Anak, and the camp lost its nerve.
Caleb said, let us go up at once.
Now, at Gilgal, he tells it in his own words, and one phrase keeps coming back: he wholly followed the Lord. He says it about himself. He quotes Moses saying it.
And the narrator says it again at the end. Then the surprise.
He says he's as strong today as the day Moses sent him, strong for war, for going out and for coming in.
And he asks: "Now therefore give me this mountain." Not a settled valley.
The hill country of Hebron, where the Anakim live, in cities great and fortified: the very people whose size frightened the scouts all those years ago. Caleb doesn't promise a victory.
He says, maybe the Lord will be with me, and I'll drive them out. The fear that froze a whole camp is the exact place he asks to go. He has carried that mountain in his mind for forty-five years.

teach.h: HEBRON IS HIS. THE LAND HAS REST.
teach.b: Joshua blesses him and gives him Hebron, and the chapter ends quietly: the land had rest from war. Some readers hear a promise finally collected, since Moses swore the land his feet walked on would be his.
Others hear something simpler: an old man who still wants a mountain to climb.

how: Jews read Caleb's request as part of Joshua, the opening book of the Prophets, and remember Caleb, with Joshua, as the scouts who did not lose heart in Numbers 13–14.

games.why: now therefore give me this mountain: the place whose giants once frightened the scouts. Joshua blesses him and gives him Hebron.

practice: Let one thing come to mind that you've put off because you told yourself it was too late, or too early: a language, an instrument, a conversation, a walk you've never taken.
Don't plan the whole mountain; just look at it, and find the very first step, small enough to take. Say Caleb's words under your breath: give me this mountain.

wordCard.voice: Anakim, the giants whose cities frightened the scouts forty-five years earlier, and whose hill country Caleb, at eighty-five, now asks Joshua to give him.

orig.note: Hebrew: this mountain, from Caleb's request in Joshua 14:12.

carryVoice: Your line: give me this mountain. Holy ground, the walls, Achan, the oath, the sun standing still, a place for everyone, and Caleb's mountain: a full week. Until tomorrow.
